summary_original: There's a question that's guided a lot of our thinking about boosters lately: What actually makes opening a booster exciting? It sounds simple. But when you sit with it long enough, it starts to reshape how you look at everything inside the wrapper. Some things that have lived in boosters for years are there because they've been there a long time, not always because they're exciting or useful. Others are there for good reasons, but those reasons aren't relevant anymore. Starting with Nauctis: The Sunken Realm , the first Magic set of 2027, we're making a series of changes to Play Boosters and Collector Boosters that reflect what we've learned about what players actually love to open. Some of these changes add things—like more opportunities to open traditional foil Japan Showcase cards or increased rare drop rates. Some remove things—like foil common and uncommon cards. All of them are in service of the same idea: Every booster you open should feel exciting and meaningful. Oh, and because it will be the first question, none of these changes come with any adjustments to prices. Our overarching goal was to make boosters more exciting to open without increasing the MSRP.
